newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet fuel prices rise on demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet fuel prices rise on demand.

text.p: Singapore oil products were firmer on Friday along with crude recovery with jet fuel leading the pack on a surge in North Asian demand, traders said.

They said Japan has been buying several jet fuel cargoes for early to mid-January arrival at over $2.00 per barrel to Singapore quotes c+f, about 50 cents over previous deals. But some traders noted that the stronger c+f Japan premiums were also due to higher freight costs. A Japanese trader sold 120,000 barrels of jet fuel to a MidEast trader at $33.30 a barrel for early January lifting fob. This was higher than Thursday's indications of $31.90 but still under the last deal of $34.20.

Traders said the high Asian prices have opened the arbitrage from the U.S. Gulf Coast and Mediterranean. They saw two Mediterranean kerosene cargoes being committed to Hong Kong for early January. Some players were also trying to ship in kerosene cargoes from the U.S. Gulf but the timing of the shipment which was for second half January might not be right to meet Japanese and S.Korean demand which was for early January, traders said.

Gas oil for early January was offered at $32.20 a barrel, above Thursday deal of $31.50. Gas oil swaps rose on continued Chinese demand with trades for January seen between $30.50 and $31.15, up from Thursday's deals of between $29.85 and 30.15.

Naphtha in Singapore failed to follow the stronger lead from crude or Tokyo's open-spec. Tight shipping and rising freight rates to north Asia capped Singapore January paper levels at $23.30/$23.40, largely unchanged from Thursday. Physical trade was thin although sellers holding barrels were starting to show cargoes as sentiment weakened. A trader said the naphtha crack for Febraury Brent/first-half Febraury open-spec was narrowing to just below $70 a tonne, compared to $76 earlier in the week. Gasoline remained steady in dull trade ahead of Monday's close of Taiwan's import tender for January-February delivery reformate. -- Singapore Newsroom (65-870 3084)
